high.title: Dollar-Won Takes Breather on Softer PCE, Closes at 1,543.10 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate closed at 1,543.10 won in overnight New York trading, edging up just 1.30 won from the prior Seoul close — a relatively contained move despite a broadly softer dollar session. The U.S. dollar index pulled back for the first time in four consecutive sessions following softer-than-expected PCE inflation data, which reduced immediate upward pressure on the pair. However, the downside for USD/KRW was also limited by month-end and half-year-end exporter dollar supply — a seasonal dynamic that typically sees Korean exporters converting foreign currency earnings, adding KRW-supportive flow into the market.

high.title: US Core PCE Price Index Rises 0.3% MoM in May, Maintaining Moderate Pace (Comprehensive)
high.summary:
The US core PCE price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.3% month-on-month in May, in line with market expectations and sustaining a moderate pace of price growth. Headline PCE came in at 0.4% MoM. For KRW/USD traders, this is a critical macro input: a benign core PCE print reduces the urgency for additional Fed tightening, which could weaken the USD broadly and provide relief to the Korean won. If the Fed reads this as confirmation of a disinflationary trend, it reinforces the case for eventual rate cuts, which would compress the US-Korea rate differential and ease pressure on the BOK to maintain a hawkish stance. Korean government bond (KTB) investors should note that a less aggressive Fed path supports duration positioning. However, the 0.4% headline reading warrants monitoring — any upside surprise in subsequent months could reignite USD strength and renewed KRW depreciation pressure. Watch for Fed commentary following this release for forward guidance signals.

---

high.title: Foreigners Snap Up Bonds Amid Sharp Market Correction - 3-Year Treasury Yield Falls 3.5bp
high.summary: South Korean government bond yields fell sharply on June 26th, with short- to medium-term maturities leading the rally. The 3-year KTB benchmark yield dropped 3.5 basis points, driven by a classic flight-to-safety bid as equity markets underwent a pronounced correction. Notably, foreign investors were active buyers of Korean bonds during the sell-off, providing a meaningful demand cushion and reinforcing the KTB market's safe-haven appeal within the EM fixed income universe. A particularly important development was a late-session sharp decline in the USD/KRW exchange rate, which market participants attributed to suspected official intervention by Korean authorities — adding a bullish overlay to the bond rally as Won strength reduces hedging costs for foreign bondholders. However, ultra-long bond yields bucked the trend and rose, weighed down by concerns over an upcoming auction. For KRW and bond traders, the key takeaways are: (1) potential BOK/MoF intervention signals a sensitivity to rapid Won depreciation, and (2) foreign buying of bonds during risk-off episodes suggests sustained demand for Korean duration. Watch the ultra-long segment closely ahead of the auction.

high.title: IRS Rates Plunge in Short to Medium Terms on Stock Correction and Won Strength
high.summary: Interest rate swap (IRS) rates fell broadly across the Korean curve on June 26th, with the most pronounced moves in the belly of the curve. The 1-year IRS declined 3.75 basis points to 3.4550%, while the 3-year and 5-year tenors dropped 5.50bp and 5.25bp respectively as of the afternoon close. Market participants cited two primary drivers: increased safe-haven buying in short-to-medium maturities as equities corrected sharply, and bullish sentiment supported by a falling dollar-won exchange rate. The convergence of equity risk-off and Won appreciation created a powerful bid for fixed-rate receivers in the swap market. For rates traders, the scale of the IRS move — particularly in the 3-5 year belly — suggests the market is beginning to price in a more dovish rates trajectory, potentially anticipating BOK easing. The alignment between cash bond yields and IRS rates falling in tandem is a constructive signal for Korean duration. Traders should monitor whether this move is sustained or reverses if equity markets stabilize and the suspected FX intervention pressure eases.

high.title: [FX Close] Won Plunges 10.70 Won on Suspected Authorities' Intervention
high.summary: The KRW staged a sharp reversal on June 26, with the USD/KRW rate closing at 1,532.00 — a drop of 10.70 won from the prior session, marking the first decline in five consecutive trading days. The move was notable given that the pair opened sharply higher at 1,547.30 (+4.60 won), suggesting initial upward momentum before being decisively overwhelmed by what market participants widely attributed to official dollar-selling intervention by Korean FX authorities.

medium.title: Chicago Fed President: 'Inflation Moving in Wrong Direction... Slight Improvement in Services Sector'
medium.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee expressed concern in a CNBC interview that U.S. inflation has "recently been moving in the wrong direction," noting the Fed has remained above its 2% target for five consecutive years. He flagged services sector inflation as particularly worrying, though acknowledged a slight improvement. For KRW and Korean bond traders, Goolsbee's hawkish tone — despite the softer PCE print — serves as a reminder that Fed rate cut expectations remain fragile. A higher-for-longer U.S. rate environment sustains carry pressure on the KRW and could weigh on Korean government bond inflows from foreign investors. Traders should monitor how other Fed speakers frame the inflation outlook heading into the July FOMC window.

medium.title: US 7-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand, Yield Meets Expectations
medium.summary: The U.S. Treasury successfully auctioned $44 billion in 7-year notes at a yield of 4.260%, down 3 basis points from the prior month's 4.290%, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.50x — slightly above the recent average, signaling healthy demand. The solid auction outcome suggests U.S. Treasury markets remain well-supported despite near-term uncertainty, which has modest implications for Korean government bond (KTB) yield spreads and relative value positioning. A well-anchored U.S. long end limits the risk of a sharp global yield spike that could pressure foreign holdings of KTBs. Fund managers should track the KTB-UST spread as a gauge of relative attractiveness for offshore bond investors.

medium.title: US and Gulf States Assert Freedom of Navigation in Hormuz Strait is 'Essential for Regional and Global Security'
medium.summary: The U.S. and the six GCC member states issued a joint statement on June 25 emphasizing the critical importance of unrestricted freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, directly opposing Iran's threatened closure. For Korea — which is heavily dependent on Middle Eastern energy imports transiting Hormuz — any escalation in the strait carries significant macro risk: higher oil prices would widen Korea's trade deficit, pressure the current account, and add depreciation risk to the KRW. The unified U.S.-GCC stance is a near-term stabilizing signal, but the situation warrants close monitoring. Energy price volatility remains a key tail risk for both the KRW and Korean inflation dynamics.

medium.title: Audit Agency to Probe Regulators Over Leveraged ETF Boom
medium.summary:
South Korea's Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) has initiated a comprehensive audit of the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), citing concerns over the proliferation of leveraged ETFs and other high-risk retail investment products amid recent market volatility. The probe focuses on the adequacy of regulatory supervision, potential mis-selling, and excessive investor costs. For international fund managers, this signals potential tightening of Korea's financial product regulatory environment, which could affect liquidity dynamics in Korean equities and derivative instruments. Any regulatory overhaul stemming from this audit could also have second-order implications for capital flows into Korean markets, particularly if retail leverage is curtailed following the recent sharp market swings.

---

medium.title: President Lee Floats Supplementary Budget for Mass GPU Procurement (Comprehensive)
medium.summary:
President Lee Jae-myung has signaled a potential supplementary budget to accelerate domestic GPU procurement, framing AI infrastructure as a national security and economic priority. While the headline focus is technology, the fiscal implications are relevant for bond market participants: additional government spending via a supplementary budget would likely require increased Korean Treasury Bond (KTB) issuance, which could exert upward pressure on yields at the short-to-medium end of the curve. Markets will be watching for any formal budget proposal size, timeline, and whether funding is sourced through new debt or reallocation. A larger-than-expected supplementary budget — on top of existing fiscal pressures — could also weigh modestly on KRW if it signals a looser fiscal stance, particularly in an environment where the BOK is carefully managing inflation and rate expectations. Investors should monitor follow-up announcements from the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

---

medium.title: FX Swap Points Rise on Month-End Won Demand
medium.summary: FX swap points moved higher across all tenors on June 26th, driven by month-end demand for Korean Won funding. The 1-year swap point closed at -14.90 Won (up 0.30 Won from the open), the 6-month at -6.80 Won (+0.20 Won), and the 3-month at -2.80 Won (+0.15 Won). The 1-month tenor also firmed modestly. While swap points remain in negative territory — reflecting the structural interest rate differential between KRW and USD — the broad-based tightening across the curve signals episodic Won demand from domestic financial institutions managing month-end FX funding needs. For FX traders, this is a technical but meaningful signal: month-end Won demand is providing a short-term floor under the currency, consistent with the broader Won strengthening observed intraday. The move also adds context to the suspected official intervention seen in the spot market — both forces aligned to push USD/KRW lower during the session. Watch for a potential reversal in swap point pressure once month-end flows subside in early July.

medium.title: Top 5 Banks' Loan-Deposit Rate Spread at 1.392% — Holds Steady from Previous Month
medium.summary: The average loan-deposit rate spread at Korea's five major banks (KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, and NH Nonghyup) stood at 1.392 percentage points in the latest monthly reading, edging up just 0.004 percentage points from the prior month — effectively flat. The data, released by the Korea Federation of Banks, is based on new household loan volumes excluding policy-based inclusive finance products. The near-unchanged spread suggests that competitive dynamics and regulatory pressure on lending margins remain in balance for now, with neither a significant widening nor compression occurring. For bond and rates investors, this is a secondary indicator of net interest margin (NIM) stability in the banking sector, which has implications for financial sector equity positions and the broader credit environment. A sustained compression in spreads could signal tightening credit conditions or policy pressure on banks to lower lending rates — a dynamic worth monitoring in the context of any future BOK rate cuts.

medium.title: Meritz Securities Issues 368 Billion Won Private Subordinated Bonds at 5.6%
medium.summary:
Meritz Securities issued 368 billion won (~$310 million) in 30-year private subordinated bonds at a coupon rate of 5.60% per annum, with an interest rate reset mechanism every five years (base rate + spread + 200bps step-up). Meritz Fire & Marine Insurance contributed 70 billion won in support of the issuance. While this is a corporate bond transaction, the pricing at 5.60% for a 30-year subordinated instrument from a domestic securities firm provides a useful market reference point for risk premium levels in Korean credit markets. The rate-reset structure with a 200bps step-up is noteworthy in the context of the current rate environment and reflects ongoing demand for yield-enhanced products among Korean institutional investors. Bond market participants should monitor whether this spread level influences broader domestic credit pricing.
